elevated CO2 and/or temperature affected seed composition and minerals in two soybean genotypes, but the effect varied depending on the genotype and the treatment.
elevated CO2 and/or temperature decreased seed composition and mineral nutrient concentrations.
the combination of elevated temperature with elevated CO2 resulted to an increase in oil, oleic acid, and sucrose, and decrease in protein, linolenic acid, and minerals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of elevated temperature and CO2 on seed quality and seed mineral nutrition, and the results are beneficial for seed production and food security.

the effects of elevated temperature and CO2 on seed quality and mineral nutrition in soybean.

elevated atmospheric CO2 concentrations and temperature affect seed composition and mineral nutrition, which are important traits related to seed production and quality.
elevated CO2 and elevated temperature affected seed composition, mineral nutrition, and 15 N and 13C dynamics in soybean genotypes.
elevated atmospheric CO2 concentrations and temperature affected seed composition and mineral nutrients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
elevated CO2 and/or high temperature can alter the seed nutritional quality and seed minerals.

elevated temperature and elevated temperature plus elevated CO2 affected soybean seed composition (protein and oil) and seed mineral nutrition (N, P, K) as well as 15N and natural abundance of 13C isotopic ratios.

the seed quality of soybean is affected by climate change, which can have an important impact on food security.
